subject: inflatable tank
title: 1,100 US Soldiers Fooled Hitler's Army With Balloons and Loudspeakers

scenes.text: In 1944, the US Army sent artists to war with balloons.
About 1,100 men: painters, designers, actors, sound engineers. Their job was to be noticed.
They inflated rubber tanks, trucks and cannons, and parked them where enemy scouts would look.
Loudspeakers played recorded tank columns that carried 15 miles. Radio operators faked the chatter of whole divisions.
From Normandy to the Rhine they staged more than 20 deceptions, posing as about 30,000 troops.
It stayed secret until 1996. The army that kept fooling the Germans was mostly air.

description:
In 1944 the US Army sent a unit of artists to the front line with inflatable tanks.
The 23rd Headquarters Special Troops, later nicknamed the Ghost Army, had about 1,100 men recruited from art schools, ad agencies and theatres; fashion designer Bill Blass and painter Ellsworth Kelly served in it. Using inflatable tanks, trucks, artillery and aircraft, recordings of armoured columns played from halftracks (audible about 15 miles away) and fake radio traffic, the unit could imitate two divisions, about 30,000 troops. It carried out more than 20 deceptions between Normandy and the Rhine in 1944 and 1945. The story stayed classified until 1996, and a law signed in February 2022 awarded the unit the Congressional Gold Medal.
Would you have fallen for it? Comment below.
first_comment: Fashion designer Bill Blass and painter Ellsworth Kelly both served in this unit. Would the trick still work today, with satellites watching?
